statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, the following holds. If there is no index j with 0 <= j < n such that the byte sequence words[j] equals the byte sequence target, then r = -1. If there is at least one such index, then r is the minimum circular distance from startIndex to an occurrence of target: r >= 0, for every such j we have r <= min(|j - startIndex|, n - |j - startIndex|), and there exists such a j with r = min(|j - startIndex|, n - |j - startIndex|), where |j - startIndex| denotes the ordinary absolute difference.
preconditions: Let n = len(words). We have 1 <= n <= 100; for every i with 0 <= i < n, len(words[i]) is between 1 and 100; every byte of every words[i] and of target is in the ASCII lowercase range 97..122; and startIndex is an integer satisfying 0 <= startIndex < n (it is passed as i64).
